title: Disorder induced time crystal in athermal random field Ising model with non-reciprocal interactions
abstract: A two species random field Ising model with non-reciprocal interactions between the species is studied using the greedy Glauber dynamics. By solving the dynamics exactly on a complete graph, we obtain the phase diagram of the model as a function of the non-reciprocal interaction ($K$) and the variance ($σ$) of the quenched random field distribution. The model exhibits a rich phase diagram with the presence of a chaotic time-oscillatory phase for intermediate values of $K$ and $σ$. The chaotic phase has stable time oscillations along with the autocorrelation time that diverges with system size on a complete graph and also in three dimensions. We find that the random field disorder along with non-reciprocal interaction alone can produce a time crystal without an external driving. In two dimensions the autocorrelation time does not increase with the system size and the time crystal phase is absent.
summary: This work analyzes a two-species random field Ising model with non-reciprocal couplings to search for intrinsic time crystal behavior. By studying the dynamics on different lattices, the authors demonstrate that disorder combined with non-reciprocity can spontaneously induce sustained, chaotic time oscillations in 3D systems without external driving. The findings map out a rich phase diagram defining this novel non-equilibrium ordered state.
main_problem: The study investigates whether a time crystal phase can spontaneously emerge in classical, out-of-equilibrium disordered systems without requiring external driving.
main_result: The model exhibits a chaotic time-oscillatory phase (a time crystal) for intermediate values of non-reciprocal interaction ($K$) and disorder variance ($\sigma$), which is absent in 2D but present in 3D on a complete graph.
method: The analysis involves solving the dynamics exactly on a complete graph, analyzing order parameter evolution via differential equations, and studying system size scaling of autocorrelation times.
model_or_system: The physical system is a two-species random field Ising model with non-reciprocal interactions ($K$) subjected to quenched Gaussian random fields ($\sigma$). The dynamics are governed by the single spin-flip greedy Glauber dynamics (GGD).
key_observables: Order parameters ($m_A, m_B$), time autocorrelation functions ($	ext{C}_{mA}(t)$), and correlation times ($	au$) showing system size dependence.
important_parameters: Non-reciprocal interaction strength ($K$), random field variance ($\sigma$), and lattice dimensionality (2D vs. 3D).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on solving dynamics exactly on a complete graph or employing mean-field approximations for the inter-species coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate free energy functionals, time evolution of magnetization showing sustained oscillations in the chaotic phase, and phase diagrams mapping the Ordered (OP), Chaotic Ordered (COP), and Disordered (DP) phases in the $K-\sigma$ plane.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the model by first establishing the dynamics on a complete graph, then constructing the phase diagram based on $(K, \sigma)$, and finally comparing results across different lattices (cubic vs. square) to confirm the robustness of the time crystal signature via $	au$ scaling.
why_interesting: The spontaneous emergence of non-equilibrium order (time crystals) in a purely classical, disordered system driven only by internal interactions is highly relevant for understanding complex dynamics outside of standard quantum driving protocols.
